sentences.en: In the evening I ate at Xiaomei's home, and Xiaomei's mom made a lot of dishes.
We had been eating for a long time, and there was still a lot of food on the table.
Xiaomei's mom brought me another dish and said: "Eat a little more!"
I said: "Thank you, but I'm really full, I can't eat any more."
Xiaomei's mom said with a smile: "Have a little more, this dish is delicious."
Xiaomei said to her mom: "Mom, he's really full, don't make him eat any more."
Mom laughed and said: "OK, then I'll go get some fruit."

quiz.q: What does the narrator say when Xiaomei's mom offers more food?
a: That the food is too spicy
That he's full and can't eat any more

quiz.q: What does Xiaomei's mom do when the narrator says he's full?
a: She insists he eat just a little more

quiz.q: What does Xiaomei's mom decide to do at the end?
a: She goes to get some fruit instead

grammar.p: 饱了 / 吃不下了 (I'm full / I can't eat any more)
grammar.e: 饱了 says you've become full; 吃不下了 says you physically can't fit any more in — both are polite ways to stop eating at a Chinese meal.
grammar.x: 我真的饱了，吃不下了。— I'm really full, I can't eat any more.

grammar.p: 再 + verb + 一点儿 (do a bit more)
grammar.e: 再 + verb + 一点儿 is what a host says to encourage a guest to eat, drink, or do something a little more.
grammar.x: 再吃一点儿，这个菜很好吃。— Have a little more, this dish is delicious.

grammar.p: 别 + 让 + person + verb + 了 (don't make someone keep doing sth)
grammar.e: 别让 + person + verb + 了 asks someone to stop making another person do something — here, stop making the guest eat more.
grammar.x: 别再让他吃了。— Don't make him eat any more.
